summary: China lets Xpeng run paid robotaxi trials in Guangzhou and VW test self-driving in Hefei, approves its first brainstem hearing implant, and a study rates Chinese video AI.
body: China is moving again on self-driving cars after a pause. Xpeng said on Monday it had received a licence to run its Yoyo robotaxis in Guangzhou with paying passengers, a trial stage operators must pass before full commercial service [^1]. Volkswagen's China business got a licence to test "Level 3" driving in Hefei, where the car drives itself in some conditions but a driver must be ready to take over [^2]. China suspended new robotaxi licences in April after an incident involving a Baidu robotaxi in Wuhan and resumed approvals in July [^2]. Xpeng aims to carry passengers without safety drivers in 2027 and is talking to European ride-hailing platforms [^1][^2].

In medicine, China's drug and device regulator approved the country's first auditory brainstem implant on Oct. 19 [^3]. It is meant for deaf children aged 2 to 6 who cannot use ordinary cochlear implants because their inner ear or hearing nerve did not form normally; it stimulates the brainstem directly [^3]. The Shanghai team that built it with a Hangzhou company told domestic media it was almost 97% effective after a year, a figure not yet independently confirmed [^3].

And a University of Hong Kong study ranked 12 AI video generators: ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 Pro scored highest for visual quality, ahead of Google's Veo 3.1 and OpenAI's Sora 2 Pro, but ranked only sixth for blocking harmful content [^4]. My read: Chinese firms are winning on quality faster than on safeguards.
